themes_detail.label: For-Hire Vehicle Surge
themes_detail.summary: For-hire vehicle complaints (Uber, Lyft, etc.) spiked to 22 THIS WEEK versus a 4.9-per-week baseline over the prior 8 weeks—a 351% jump (z-score: 9.34)—suggesting a sudden surge in congestion, illegal parking, or passenger behavior issues in Sunnyside/Woodside.
evidence: 22 for-hire vehicle complaints THIS WEEK vs. 4.9 per-week average over prior 8 weeks (351% increase)
Z-score of 9.34 indicates statistically significant anomaly
Illegal Parking remains top complaint category district-wide (6,068 over 90 days), suggesting FHV overlap
reporting_angles: Interview residents and local business owners about FHV congestion and illegal parking on residential streets
Investigate whether FHV companies are directing drivers to Sunnyside/Woodside due to reduced enforcement or lower rates vs. Manhattan

themes_detail.label: Outdoor Dining Complaints Spike
themes_detail.summary: Outdoor dining complaints jumped to 6 THIS WEEK from a 0.2-per-week baseline—a 2,300% spike (z-score: 13.28)—indicating possible expansion of street dining without proper permits, noise, or sanitation issues in the district.
evidence: 6 outdoor dining complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 per-week average over prior 8 weeks (2,300% increase)
Z-score of 13.28 indicates extreme statistical anomaly
Noise - Park complaints also up 833% this week (7 vs. 0.8 avg), suggesting activity concentration in public spaces
reporting_angles: Map which restaurants or blocks have triggered complaints; determine if new dining permits were recently issued
Examine whether outdoor dining expansion is unregulated or if SLA/DOH enforcement has lagged

themes_detail.label: Park Noise Escalation
themes_detail.summary: Park noise complaints spiked to 7 THIS WEEK from a 0.8-per-week baseline—an 833% jump (z-score: 9.45)—potentially linked to unsupervised events, street dining expansion, or heavy foot traffic in Sunnyside/Woodside parks.
evidence: 7 park noise complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.8 per-week average over prior 8 weeks (833% increase)
Z-score of 9.45 indicates strong statistical significance
Outdoor Dining spike (6 complaints this week) may be contributing factor; community board budget requests note lack of park amenities/investment
reporting_angles: Identify which parks are generating complaints (Sunnyside Park, Gantry Park, etc.); determine source (music, crowds, events, street vendors)
Interview Parks Dept. about event permits, programming, and noise enforcement capacity

themes_detail.label: Tree Damage and Canopy Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Dead/Dying Tree complaints jumped to 7 LAST WEEK (5,500% spike, z-score: 20.79) and Illegal Tree Damage complaints rose to 4 TWO WEEKS AGO (433% spike, z-score: 7.51)—totaling 11 tree-related complaints in 2 weeks versus near-zero baseline, suggesting either environmental damage, development impact, or contractor negligence.
evidence: Dead/Dying Tree: 7 complaints last week vs. 0.1 per-week average (5,500% increase, z-score: 20.79)
Illegal Tree Damage: 4 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.8 per-week average (433% increase, z-score: 7.51)
675 DOB building permits filed in last 90 days (466 alterations + 107 new buildings) may indicate construction-related tree damage; 4 active rezonings in pipeline suggest ongoing development pressure
reporting_angles: Cross-reference tree damage complaints with active construction sites and permit locations; investigate whether contractors are violating tree protection ordinances
Interview Parks Dept. and DEC about canopy loss and whether climate/environmental factors are also accelerating tree die-off

themes_detail.label: Sanitation and Illegal Dumping Uptick
themes_detail.summary: Illegal Dumping complaints surged to 27 TWO WEEKS AGO (188% above 8-week average of 9.4, z-score: 5.2) and Litter Basket Requests jumped to 5 LAST WEEK (1,900% spike, z-score: 7.18)—together signaling deteriorating street conditions and possible lack of waste infrastructure.
evidence: Illegal Dumping: 27 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 9.4 per-week average (188% increase, z-score: 5.2)
Litter Basket Requests: 5 complaints last week vs. 0.2 per-week average (1,900% increase, z-score: 7.18)
Street Condition remains elevated at 1,422 complaints over 90 days; community board has repeated budget requests for 'Other capital budget request for DEP,' indicating persistent infrastructure gap
reporting_angles: Map dumping hotspots in Sunnyside/Woodside; interview DSNY about collection frequency and capacity
Investigate whether gentrification or rapid development is driving contractor/illegal waste disposal
